== Olympic Winter Games, not Winter Olympic Games ==

The correct, [https://ita.sport/partner/international-olympic-committee-ioc/ official name] of these games is the "Olympic Winter Games", not the "Winter Olympic Games", which [https://www.olympics.com/ioc/news/the-first-olympic-winter-games-of-them-all has been the case] [http://isoh.org/wp-content/uploads/JOH-Archives/JOHv2n2h.pdf since 1926]. Aside from it being the correct official name, there is an important distinction in the Winter Games versus the Summer Games (more commonly known as the 'Olympic Games'). IMO the article should be retitled accordingly, likewise all internal references throughout the article should be amended. '''''[[user:Christopherwoods|Chris W.]]''' [[user_talk:Christopherwoods|(talk)]]'' 03:35, 8 February 2026 (UTC)

::What reliable sources are you referring to? I would contend those are incorrect usages, and may be conflating things like "Winter Olympics" and "Winter Olympic Games". The former is fine, the latter isn't.
::Use of "Winter Olympic Games" notwithstanding, Wikipedia itself takes great care to always include the official name in articles for each respective OWG (e.g. from the 2030 article: The '''2030 Winter Olympics''' ([[French language|French]]: ''Jeux olympiques d'hiver de 2030''), officially known as the '''XXVI Olympic Winter Games''' ([[French language|French]]: ''XXVI<sup>es</sup> Jeux Olympiques d'hiver'')). 
::Google refers to it as the Olympic Winter Games. The organising body does not refer to it as the 'Winter Olympic Games', only the 'Olympic Winter Games'. Officially it is either the "Winter Olympics" or the "Olympic Winter Games" (the IOC's trademarked both).
::My opinion is that Wikipedia should reflect the correct, official name as the article title, with redirects for "Winter Olympics" and "Winter Olympic Games". The article can certainly reference unofficial but popular derivations, but should be clear that the official names are either "Winter Olympics" or the "Olympic Winter Games". The official names are ''Olympic Winter Games™'', ''Paralympic Winter Games™'', ''Winter Olympics™'' and so on (as evidenced by reliable sources like the OWG26 site - https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/territories). ==GA Reassessment==
{{Wikipedia:Good article reassessment/Winter Olympic Games/1}}

== Olympic Winter Games, not Winter Olympic Games ==

The correct, [https://ita.sport/partner/international-olympic-committee-ioc/ official name] of these games is the "Olympic Winter Games", not the "Winter Olympic Games", which [https://www.olympics.com/ioc/news/the-first-olympic-winter-games-of-them-all has been the case] [http://isoh.org/wp-content/uploads/JOH-Archives/JOHv2n2h.pdf since 1926]. Aside from it being the correct official name, there is an important distinction in the Winter Games versus the Summer Games (more commonly known as the 'Olympic Games'). IMO the article should be retitled accordingly, likewise all internal references throughout the article should be amended. '''''[[user:Christopherwoods|Chris W.]]''' [[user_talk:Christopherwoods|(talk)]]'' 03:35, 8 February 2026 (UTC)

::What reliable sources are you referring to? I would contend those are incorrect usages, and may be conflating things like "Winter Olympics" and "Winter Olympic Games". The former is fine, the latter isn't.
::Use of "Winter Olympic Games" notwithstanding, Wikipedia itself takes great care to always include the official name in articles for each respective OWG (e.g. from the 2030 article: The '''2030 Winter Olympics''' ([[French language|French]]: ''Jeux olympiques d'hiver de 2030''), officially known as the '''XXVI Olympic Winter Games''' ([[French language|French]]: ''XXVI<sup>es</sup> Jeux Olympiques d'hiver'')). 
::Google refers to it as the Olympic Winter Games. The organising body does not refer to it as the 'Winter Olympic Games', only the 'Olympic Winter Games'. Officially it is either the "Winter Olympics" or the "Olympic Winter Games" (the IOC's trademarked both).
::My opinion is that Wikipedia should reflect the correct, official name as the article title, with redirects for "Winter Olympics" and "Winter Olympic Games". The article can certainly reference unofficial but popular derivations, but should be clear that the official names are either "Winter Olympics" or the "Olympic Winter Games". The official names are ''Olympic Winter Games™'', ''Paralympic Winter Games™'', ''Winter Olympics™'' and so on (as evidenced by reliable sources like the OWG26 site - https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/territories). ::What reliable sources are you referring to? I would contend those are incorrect usages, and may be conflating things like "Winter Olympics" and "Winter Olympic Games". The former is fine, the latter isn't.
::Use of "Winter Olympic Games" notwithstanding, Wikipedia itself takes great care to always include the official name in articles for each respective OWG (e.g. from the 2030 article: The '''2030 Winter Olympics''' ([[French language|French]]: ''Jeux olympiques d'hiver de 2030''), officially known as the '''XXVI Olympic Winter Games''' ([[French language|French]]: ''XXVI<sup>es</sup> Jeux Olympiques d'hiver'')). 
::Google refers to it as the Olympic Winter Games. The organising body does not refer to it as the 'Winter Olympic Games', only the 'Olympic Winter Games'. Officially it is either the "Winter Olympics" or the "Olympic Winter Games" (the IOC's trademarked both).
::My opinion is that Wikipedia should reflect the correct, official name as the article title, with redirects for "Winter Olympics" and "Winter Olympic Games". The article can certainly reference unofficial but popular derivations, but should be clear that the official names are either "Winter Olympics" or the "Olympic Winter Games". The official names are ''Olympic Winter Games™'', ''Paralympic Winter Games™'', ''Winter Olympics™'' and so on (as evidenced by reliable sources like the OWG26 site - https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/territories). '''''[[user:Christopherwoods|Chris W.]]''' [[user_talk:Christopherwoods|(talk)]]'' 12:17, 17 February 2026 (UTC)

The correct, [https://ita.sport/partner/international-olympic-committee-ioc/ official name] of these games is the "Olympic Winter Games", not the "Winter Olympic Games", which [https://www.olympics.com/ioc/news/the-first-olympic-winter-games-of-them-all has been the case] [http://isoh.org/wp-content/uploads/JOH-Archives/JOHv2n2h.pdf since 1926]. Aside from it being the correct official name, there is an important distinction in the Winter Games versus the Summer Games (more commonly known as the 'Olympic Games'). IMO the article should be retitled accordingly, likewise all internal references throughout the article should be amended. '''''[[user:Christopherwoods|Chris W.]]''' [[user_talk:Christopherwoods|(talk)]]'' 03:35, 8 February 2026 (UTC)

kind.description: They propose renaming Olympic and television studio articles to match official names, citing Olympic organizations’ websites and names used in related Wikipedia articles. They argue official names should take priority over popular alternatives. They also offer their own recent photograph of a transmitting mast to show equipment changes, asking whether it should replace an older image.

::What reliable sources are you referring to? I would contend those are incorrect usages, and may be conflating things like "Winter Olympics" and "Winter Olympic Games". The former is fine, the latter isn't.
::Use of "Winter Olympic Games" notwithstanding, Wikipedia itself takes great care to always include the official name in articles for each respective OWG (e.g. from the 2030 article: The '''2030 Winter Olympics''' ([[French language|French]]: ''Jeux olympiques d'hiver de 2030''), officially known as the '''XXVI Olympic Winter Games''' ([[French language|French]]: ''XXVI<sup>es</sup> Jeux Olympiques d'hiver'')). 
::Google refers to it as the Olympic Winter Games. The organising body does not refer to it as the 'Winter Olympic Games', only the 'Olympic Winter Games'. Officially it is either the "Winter Olympics" or the "Olympic Winter Games" (the IOC's trademarked both).
::My opinion is that Wikipedia should reflect the correct, official name as the article title, with redirects for "Winter Olympics" and "Winter Olympic Games". The article can certainly reference unofficial but popular derivations, but should be clear that the official names are either "Winter Olympics" or the "Olympic Winter Games". The official names are ''Olympic Winter Games™'', ''Paralympic Winter Games™'', ''Winter Olympics™'' and so on (as evidenced by reliable sources like the OWG26 site - https://www.olympics.com/en/milano-cortina-2026/territories). '''''[[user:Christopherwoods|Chris W.]]''' [[user_talk:Christopherwoods|(talk)]]'' 12:17, 17 February 2026 (UTC)
examples.discussion_title: Olympic Winter Games, not Winter Olympic Games

== dock10 renamed to MediaCity Studios And Post ==
In 2026 just prior to the World Cup, dock10 formally renamed to "MediaCity Studios and Post", though a few colloquial references to 'dock10' or 'studio block' persist in documentation or parts of the MCUK web site. == More recent photo of the mast, taken in less favourable weather - worth adding or not? ==

I took a high resolution composite of the mast from the summit in March 2025 (https://www.flickr.com/photos/christopherw/54414564736/in/datetaken-public/) which I'd be happy to CC and add to this article, in place of the older image dated 2015. There have been various changes to the equipment on the mast in the intervening decade. However the weather was not ideal when I was up there, so my photo is not as vivid as the 2015 image. Does anyone have any opinion on if it's worth updating the article with it? '''''[[user:Christopherwoods|Chris W.]]''' [[user_talk:Christopherwoods|(talk)]]'' 15:19, 13 February 2026 (UTC)
